Messages.Author: Murcalumis
Messages.Body:
once more for the record: how does one burn a wake? here's a scenario:
wynn, who my predator controls, uses his special ability to rush one of my
vamps at +1 stealth. there is no way of me gaining +1 intercept but i
still play a wake on a tapped vamp (not the one wynn is rushing). when
_exactly_ is the wake replaced? as soon as the waking vamp cannot gain +1
intercept or as soon as the combat is over between wynn and my rushed
vamp? thanks in advance...

--V--V-- simulacrum

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
murca...@aol.com (Murcalumis) writes:

>once more for the record: how does one burn a wake? here's a scenario:
>wynn, who my predator controls, uses his special ability to rush one of my
>vamps at +1 stealth. there is no way of me gaining +1 intercept but i
>still play a wake on a tapped vamp (not the one wynn is rushing). when
>_exactly_ is the wake replaced? as soon as the waking vamp cannot gain +1
>intercept or as soon as the combat is over between wynn and my rushed
>vamp? thanks in advance...

Any wake played (by any vampire - blocking or no) is replaced after the
next ensuing combat is ended, or after the current action is ended,
whichever comes first.
--

This is a seemingly simple question, but kind of throny. I think the
common sense answer is that the wording of wake mean's(ie should be) If
the action is blocked and combat occurs, do not replace wake until after combat.
In which case it would be replaced as soon as the block did not take place.

There may have been an official ruling to this effect but I am not sure. Anyone?

--Steve
